response.evidence: The dataset contains about 22 applications from Black or African American female applicants. 20 were originated and 2 were denied, a denial rate of roughly 9%. This is broadly similar to the overall denial rate in the dataset, which appears to be about 9-10% based on an approximate count. Both denials had high-risk profiles: debt-to-income ratio of 50%-60%, loan-to-value ratio of 97, and relatively low income (90 and 63). White, Hispanic and Asian applicants with similar high debt-to-income ratios were also frequently denied. A third Black female applicant in the 50%-60% debt-to-income range was approved. Black female applicants with debt-to-income ratios at or below 49% were all approved, including several with loan-to-value ratios of 95-97.66. Confidence is moderate because the subgroup is small, the data cannot rule out subtler effects such as pricing or terms, and credit history and other underwriting factors are not included.
